results: PeriodOneMassSobolevInverse proves that the original massive inverse symbol gains ONE full Sobolev order at EVERY real order and every Banach exponent, uniformly in mass, retaining all raw coefficients. Its L2-to-H1 form uses the original period-one 2*pi*i*k symbol.

AnalyticMiuraExponentRecovery gives an explicit analytic polynomial L2 x L2 -> ell^(4/3), using the fixed massive kernel, Holder and Young maps. Whenever v satisfies the original weak Miura equation v' + v*v = q, EVERY recovered coefficient is exactly v_k.

AnalyticMiuraH1Recovery gives an explicit entire complex analytic H1 representative from L2 forcing and an L2 weak solution. The original equation proves coefficientwise identity and equality under the original scalar inclusion. Stronger-norm analyticity is PROVED by bounded formulas, rather than inferred from pointwise regularity.

AnalyticMiuraSmoothingRemainder constructs the analytic H2 polynomial M^-1(u-u*u) for H1 lifts. Under the original weak equation its ENTIRE raw sequence is u_k - M(k)^-1*q_k. H1 convolution is the existing actual bounded Sobolev algebra product.

HillMiuraL2AnalyticRegularity applies the explicit recovery to EVERY actual Hill Miura action ball on its complex L2 source preimage. Its H1 lift is analytic and equals the SAME original rough lift in every coefficient. The H2 remainder after M^-1 times q plus the ORIGINAL fixed energy shift is analytic, with exact raw identity.

HillRotatedDiracL2Regularity proves that the SAME phase-rotated Dirac source used by the actual Hill spectral-core bridge has an analytic H1 representative on the actual complex L2 patch preimage. The original Sobolev inclusion yields the entire original two-component source, with phases +i and -i unchanged.

This closes the actual analytic Miura/rotated-source H1 input obligation for the L2 native smoothing route. It does NOT prove terminal-coordinate, normalized-amplitude or signed off-index one-smoothing. Actual native base smoothing and Main5.1/5.9 remain OPEN; Main1.1/1.3/1.4 remain proved.
